title: AND conjunction semantics — Boolean Search
description: AND requires every listed condition to hold, so each added term can only shrink the result set, never grow it. Evaluators intersect term postings or test set membership per document, typically starting with the rarest term to fail fast. AND is the workhorse of precision: users add terms until the result set is small enough to inspect.

title: OR disjunction semantics — Boolean Search
description: OR accepts documents matching any listed condition, so each added term can only grow the result set. Evaluators union postings lists or test membership against any of several term sets. OR is the workhorse of recall: users add synonyms and spelling variants to catch everything relevant.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: NOT negation semantics — Boolean Search
description: NOT excludes documents matching a condition, and it binds tighter than AND and OR in the standard precedence. Evaluators compute the complement of a term's postings against the full document universe, or simply reject documents containing the term. NOT is how users carve noise out of broad queries without rephrasing the positive conditions.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Parenthesized grouping — Boolean Search
description: Parentheses override default precedence so that 'a AND (b OR c)' means something different from '(a AND b) OR c'. Parsers treat '(' by pushing it on the operator stack and ')' by popping operators until the matching '(' appears. Grouping is the only way to express mixed logic faithfully, and query UIs that hide it confuse advanced users.

title: Operator precedence rules — Boolean Search
description: The conventional precedence is NOT first, then AND, then OR, mirroring arithmetic's unary-minus, multiplication, and addition. The shunting-yard algorithm encodes this with a precedence table, emitting operators to postfix order whenever a higher-or-equal precedence operator sits atop the stack. Documenting precedence in the UI prevents the classic surprise where 'a OR b AND c' behaves as 'a OR (b AND c)'.

title: De Morgan transformations — Boolean Search
description: De Morgan's laws rewrite 'NOT (a AND b)' as '(NOT a) OR (NOT b)' and 'NOT (a OR b)' as '(NOT a) AND (NOT b)'. Query optimizers push NOT inward to the leaves, turning expensive complement operations into cheap term-level exclusions. Normalized negation form also simplifies caching, since more queries share identical subexpressions.

title: Distributive rewriting — Boolean Search
description: AND distributes over OR, so 'a AND (b OR c)' equals '(a AND b) OR (a AND c)'. Engines expand to disjunctive normal form when the index only supports conjunctive postings access, or keep the factored form when the planner can share the 'a' evaluation. The choice affects both plan shape and cache reuse across subqueries.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tautology and contradiction detection — Boolean Search
description: A query like 'a AND NOT a' can never match, while 'a OR NOT a' always matches; both are detectable statically. Simplifiers apply absorption ('a AND (a OR b)' = 'a') and complement laws during parsing, before any postings are touched. Early simplification saves whole index scans and gives users immediate feedback on impossible queries.

title: Short-circuit evaluation — Boolean Search
description: Conjunctions evaluate left to right and stop at the first false term; disjunctions stop at the first true term. Ordering terms by increasing selectivity (rarest first for AND, commonest first for OR) minimizes the expected work. Short-circuiting is why term statistics are collected at index time: they drive the evaluation order.

title: Three-valued logic with missing fields — Boolean Search
description: When a document lacks the queried field, strict true/false logic misleads; Kleene three-valued logic adds UNKNOWN. Comparisons against missing values yield UNKNOWN, and AND/OR truth tables extend naturally: TRUE AND UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN. Explicit unknown-handling keeps fielded boolean search honest on ragged real-world records.

title: Boolean query optimization — Boolean Search
description: Optimizers reorder conjuncts by estimated selectivity, hoist common subexpressions, and drop redundant terms. Selectivity comes from document frequencies stored in the index: rarer terms are evaluated first under AND. A good plan can run orders of magnitude faster than naive left-to-right evaluation on the same query.

title: Nested boolean trees — Boolean Search
description: Real queries nest arbitrarily: '((a OR b) AND NOT c) OR (d AND e)'. Parsers build an expression tree where leaves are term tests and interior nodes are operators, then evaluate bottom-up per document or per postings list. Tree form also enables subexpression caching across queries in a session.

title: Boolean retrieval model theory — Boolean Search
description: The classic boolean retrieval model treats documents as sets of terms and queries as set expressions, returning unranked matching sets. Its strength is predictable, explainable semantics: a document matches if and only if the expression is true. Its weakness, no ranking, is why modern systems layer scoring on top while keeping boolean structure for filtering.

title: Extended boolean with weights — Boolean Search
description: Extended boolean models soften the all-or-nothing semantics by weighting terms and using p-norm combination of AND/OR. With p=1 the model behaves like a vector sum; as p grows it approaches strict boolean logic. This gives users boolean control with ranked output, the best of both retrieval worlds.

title: Query debugging and explanation — Boolean Search
description: Explain plans show which subexpression matched each document, so users can see why a result appeared. Debuggers highlight the terms that fired per document and report per-clause match counts. Transparent boolean evaluation turns 'why is this here?' from a mystery into a one-glance answer.
